problem: Image generation models often exhibit local distortions, structural inconsistencies in complex objects, poor multi-object interactions, and failure modes when handling underrepresented data (p.2). Existing image-level retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) methods use static, coarse-grained retrievals before generation, leading to issues like over-copying irrelevant details, stylistic bias, and hallucinations (p.2).
methodology: The paper introduces Autoregressive Retrieval Augmentation (AR-RAG), a paradigm that dynamically incorporates patch-level k-nearest-neighbor retrievals step-by-step using prior-generated surrounding patches as queries (p.2). It proposes two parallel implementations: (1) Distribution-Augmentation in Decoding (DAiD), a training-free strategy merging the model's predicted patch distribution with retrieved patch distributions using l2 distance and softmax probabilities (p.2, p.4), and (2) Feature-Augmentation in Decoding (FAiD), a parameter-efficient fine-tuning approach that uses multi-scale convolutions to smooth retrieved patch features and blends them with model representations using learned compatibility scores (p.2, p.4-5).
dataset: The patch-based retrieval database is constructed using 5.7 million images from CC12M, 3.3 million from JourneyDB, and 4.6 million from DataComp, while models are fine-tuned on 50,000 image-caption pairs from CC12M and Midjourney-v6 (p.6). Benchmarks used for evaluation include Midjourney-30K, GenEval, and DPG-Bench (p.6).
results: AR-RAG consistently outperforms existing non-retrieval and retrieval-augmented methods across benchmarks, establishing new state-of-the-art results for comparable autoregressive models (p.6, p.7). For instance, Janus-Pro with FAiD achieves 6.67 FID on Midjourney-30K and an overall score of 0.78 on GenEval (p.3).
key_findings: Autoregressive patch-level retrieval successfully addresses the over-copying and irrelevance issues of static, full-image RAG methods by responding to evolving generation needs and local context (p.2, p.7). DAiD and FAiD improve spatial coherence, structural integrity, and multi-object generation without introducing heavy computational overhead (p.3, p.7).
title: AR-RAG: Autoregressive Retrieval Augmentation for Image Generation
